matchstick.title: Move vertical I-stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: If the numeric discrepancy can be fixed by adding or removing a value of 1, move a single vertical stick that forms an I from one numeral to another to adjust the values.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by a small amount (±1) and a vertical stick can be transferred between numerals to balance it.
matchstick.example: Removing a vertical stick from an I without placing it elsewhere, leaving an empty character.

matchstick.title: Prefer intra-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: First try to fix the equation by moving a stick within the same character (e.g., turning X into V) before considering moves that affect other characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, before attempting any inter‑character relocations.
matchstick.example: Skipping intra‑character changes like X→V and directly moving sticks between characters, missing a simpler solution.

matchstick.title: Validate symbols after stick move
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, ensure every resulting character is a recognized Roman numeral or operator; discard any configuration that leaves an invalid symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after each candidate move, before evaluating the arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Leaving a lone diagonal stick as a character, which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Avoid single angled sticks
matchstick.principle: A single diagonal stick does not represent any Roman numeral; angled sticks must appear in valid pairs (e.g., V, X).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a move creates or removes an angled stick, check that the resulting character still contains a valid pair of diagonals.
matchstick.example: Turning X into a single diagonal line, which is not a recognized numeral.

matchstick.title: Convert plus to minus by removing vertical stick
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into a minus sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a plus sign and converting it to minus could help balance the arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from '+' to make '-', but not using the removed stick elsewhere.

matchstick.title: Create new numeral by reordering stick
matchstick.principle: A detached stick can be placed as a separate character to form a new valid Roman numeral (e.g., moving a vertical stick to create an I).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a move leaves a free stick, consider using it to form a new numeral rather than discarding it.
matchstick.example: Leaving a detached stick unused after a move, rather than forming a new numeral.

matchstick.title: Consider inter-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If no intra‑character move yields a valid equality, explore moving a stick from one character to another, possibly creating or modifying numerals or operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting all intra‑character options without success.
matchstick.example: Only trying intra‑character changes and never considering moving a stick between characters, missing the correct solution.

matchstick.title: Augment numeral with vertical stick from operator
matchstick.principle: After converting a plus sign to a minus by removing its vertical stick, attach that stick to a nearby numeral to increase its value.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a plus sign is present and converting it to minus leaves a vertical stick that can be used to augment a numeral.
matchstick.example: Converting '+' to '-' and forgetting to attach the removed vertical stick to a numeral, leaving an invalid configuration.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic after stick move
matchstick.principle: After forming new Roman numerals and operators, compute their numeric values to ensure the equation holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each candidate transformation, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Accepting a visually valid equation without checking that the numeric values actually match.

matchstick.title: Swap operators by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: When an equation contains both an equals sign and a minus sign, moving a single horizontal stick from the equals sign to the minus sign (or vice versa) swaps their functions, turning '=' into '-' and '-' into '=', which can correct the arithmetic.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the numeric discrepancy suggests that exchanging the roles of '=' and '-' could balance the equation, and both operators are present, consider moving a horizontal stick between them.
matchstick.example: Changing '=' to '-' by removing a horizontal stick but not placing that stick onto the '-' sign, leaving an extra stick unused.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model jumps to moving sticks between characters because inter‑character moves appear more obvious, neglecting simpler intra‑character changes that could solve the puzzle.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Systematically try all possible intra‑character stick relocations (e.g., X→V, V→X, I→L) before considering inter‑character moves.

matchstick.description: Assuming sticks retain their orientation and not rotating horizontals to verticals (or vice versa) when repositioning
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats sticks as immutable in orientation, missing valid transformations that involve rotating a stick when it is placed elsewhere.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Remember that a stick can be reoriented when relocated; consider both its shape and possible new orientation in every move.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on visual validity of symbols and forgets to check whether the resulting Roman numerals satisfy the equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any move, compute the decimal values of both sides and verify equality before accepting the solution.

matchstick.description: Assuming operator swaps (e.g., = ↔ -) automatically solve the puzzle
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may think that simply exchanging the symbols fixes the equation, overlooking the requirement to move a stick rather than replace symbols.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure that any operator change is achieved by moving a stick, and that the removed stick is placed elsewhere to keep the total stick count unchanged.

matchstick.description: Forgetting to place the removed stick after modifying an operator (e.g., converting plus to minus) and leaving it unused
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes removes a stick from an operator to change its type but does not relocate that stick, violating the rule that exactly one stick must be moved.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After altering an operator, immediately decide where the removed stick will go, ensuring it creates a valid numeral or operator.
